composition.structure: Additive phase-5 layer over boss_mang_cot (10 bars @ 66 bpm): 16th-note drum ticks on the 'e'/'a' subdivisions (the grid phases 2/3/4 leave free), 16th-note bass alternating D1/D2 (phases 2/3 drive 8th-note D1, phase 4 drives 8th-note D1/D2), high D6 bell toll every bar (phase 4 tolls it every 2 bars), and the minor-head fragment in FLUTE on bars 0 and 8 (the boss theme lifted to a scream register -- the first flute in any boss layer; the base has no flute at all, so the voice is new. Bar 0 doubles phase 3's pluck fragment in the new voice; bar 8 answers the base's own foreign FS5 bell and variant fragment). No pad. -25 LUFS target; combined base+layer loudness measured from real bytes.

notes: Phase layers are ADDITIVE loops at the parent cue's tempo/bars (-25 LUFS target): they play over the base cue, they do not replace it. Combined base+layer loudness/true-peak is measured from real bytes and recorded per layer.

Each MD5 layer adds only what its base and the earlier layers do not already do: boss phase 5 completes the 16th-note drum grid with 16th-note octave bass, a D6 bell every bar and the minor head in flute (the first flute in any boss layer -- the base has no flute at all); hub intensity adds the festival pulse a drumless home base withholds; rain intensity adds the weight of heavier rain inside the base's own 1200 Hz veil.

Adoption is a presentation-adapter decision (Codex): the MD5 files are delivered in parallel under ClientGodot/assets/audio/composed/layers/ and do NOT replace the ported PackV1 files, their cue bindings, or the checkpoint-26/30/MD1/MD2/MD3/MD4 cues.

No ear audition has been done; loudness/true-peak are measured from real bytes. Loop seams are recorded per looping cue in the delivery manifest: wrapJump after a disclosed 0.25 s end-landing loop construction, wrapJumpRaw before it.
